decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Progress on vaccinations has reduced the spread of COVID-19 in the United States.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this new sentence to acknowledge that vaccinations are helping slow the spread of the virus.

changes.quote: Amid this progress and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened.
changes.explanation: Language was updated to note that economic activity and employment are strengthening alongside vaccination progress.

changes.quote: The COVID-19 pandemic is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world.
changes.explanation: The Committee removed this reference to the tremendous hardship caused by the pandemic, reflecting improving conditions.

changes.quote: Progress on vaccinations will likely continue to reduce the effects of the public health crisis on the economy, but risks to the economic outlook remain.
changes.explanation: The Fed replaced older text about the crisis weighing on the economy with a more forward-looking statement on vaccination effects and remaining risks.

changes.quote: With inflation having run persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent.
changes.explanation: A minor wording update was made regarding inflation running persistently below the longer-run goal.

tone_quotes.quote: Amid this progress and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened.
Inflation has risen, largely reflecting transitory factors.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.75% APR costs about $61.46 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.57% and moved +6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 2.99% would rise by about $9.72 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5.8%, and employers added an average of 562k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4.9% over the past year (May 2021); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 6.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +5 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.54%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.21% on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed will likely maintain its current policy stance until substantial further progress is made toward maximum employment and price stability. The educational forecast model indicates a 90% chance of a hold at the next meeting.
